interpretation: The pooled positive richness-retention gradient is not robust after stable-transect saturation. Higher source richness may partly mark persistently favorable transects rather than a purely microsite-scale biodiversity-insurance mechanism.
claim_boundary: Post-hoc reference-saturation audit of an already-opened richness endpoint.
Do not call the pooled richness gradient causal biodiversity insurance after the within-node interval overlaps zero.
The positive within-node point estimate remains descriptive and does not replace the failed support rule.
Persistent site quality can jointly increase local richness and later seagrass retention.
Retention of any seagrass does not imply equivalent ecosystem function after Thalassia loss.
